operators.name: At
operators.description:
Access an element of an indexed collection.

If the index is negative, it is counted from the end.

Multiple indices can be provided to access nested collections (e.g., matrices).

If the index is a finite collection of booleans, returns the elements where the mask is True (a mask is a filter, and its length must match the collection length; otherwise it is an error).

If the index is a finite collection of integers, returns the elements at those indices, preserving position: an out-of-range index yields the absence marker, it is not dropped.

Out-of-band access (an out-of-range index, or a dictionary key that is not present) yields a POSITION-PRESERVING marker: `NaN` when the collection’s elements are numeric, `Missing` otherwise. It never yields `Nothing`, which would erase the position.

operators.name: Block
operators.description:
Evaluate a sequence of expressions in a local scope, **sequentially**. Each operand is evaluated in order; later operands observe side effects (`Assign`, `Declare`) of earlier operands. The block's value is the value of the last expression. Short-circuiting heads (`Return`, `Break`, `Continue`) terminate the sequence early.

IMPORTANT — consumers translating *simultaneous* action tuples (e.g. Desmos `(a → 1, b → a + 1)` where `b` reads the *pre-action* `a`) must rewrite to a snapshot-then-commit Block: bind each RHS to a fresh temp first, then assign the temps to the LHS symbols. See `docs/architecture/actions-and-randomness.md` for the canonical recipe.

operators.name: Declare
operators.signature: (symbol, type: (string | symbol)?, value: any?, attributes: dictionary<any>?) scope -> any
operators.description: Declare a symbol in the current scope, optionally assigning a type and an initial value. An optional trailing attributes dictionary (with keys `type`, `value`, `constant` and `holdUntil`) can further describe the definition, e.g. to declare a constant. With a value, evaluates to that value; otherwise evaluates to `Nothing`.

operators.name: DeclareConformance
operators.signature: (target: string|symbol, protocols: any, whereClauseOrImplementation: any?, implementation: dictionary<any>?) scope -> nothing
operators.description: Declare that a type CONFORMS to one or more protocols — the lowering of the Epsil `type string is Hashable & Comparable` statement. The target rides as a type-expression string and must be named and ground (not a union, an anonymous structural type or a `type alias` name); the protocols ride as a `List` of names. An optional trailing dictionary carries the implementation block, member name -> function literal (property handlers under the mangled keys `__get__x` / `__set__x`); it may only accompany a SINGLE protocol. A CONDITIONAL conformance carries, ahead of that block, the source text of its trailing `where` clause as a string: the target is then a head pattern naming the variables the clause binds (`list<T>` with `"where T is Comparable"`). Conformance is monotone — it can be added but never removed — and a re-declaration is a no-op. Evaluates to `Nothing`.

operators.name: DeclareProtocol
operators.description: Declare a PROTOCOL: a set of function and property requirements a type may declare itself to satisfy. Protocols are engine-global (not lexically scoped) and are NOT types, so this is only valid at the top level of a program. The name is a symbol (or a string); the optional members ride as a dictionary of `member -> ["Pair", "function"|"readonly"|"readwrite", signature]`, with the signature as a type-expression string. A `function` member's first parameter must be typed `Self`, the substitution token standing for the conforming type. A protocol with no members is a SEMANTIC protocol (a marker). Evaluates to `Nothing`.

operators.name: DeclareSumType
operators.description: Declare a SUM TYPE: N nominal variants plus the transparent union that names them, in one statement — the lowering of the Epsil sugar `type node = lit(num: number) | plus(op1: node, op2: node)`. The name is a symbol (or a string); each variant is a `["Tuple", name, payload]` pair whose payload is a type string (`"nothing"` for a nullary variant). An optional attributes dictionary at operand 1 — ahead of the variants — carries `typeParams -> "T"` for a generic sum, whose parameters are distributed to each variant by usage. The sum name is forward-registered before the variants are declared, so a payload may name it bare. A variant name that already names a type, is reserved, or is a builtin is rejected and NOTHING is declared. Types are engine-global, so this is only valid at the top level of a program. Evaluates to `Nothing`.

operators.name: DeclareType
operators.signature: (symbol|string, type: string|symbol, attributes: dictionary<any>?) scope -> nothing
operators.description: Declare a type. Types are engine-global (not lexically scoped), so this is only valid at the top level of a program — inside a block or function body it is an error. The name is a symbol (or a string) and the type a string holding a type expression, e.g. `"tuple<x: integer, y: integer>"`. The type is nominal by default; an optional trailing attributes dictionary with `alias -> True` makes it a structural alias instead, and an additional `typeParams -> "T, U: number"` entry makes it a GENERIC alias whose uses must be applied (`Pair<integer>`). The declaration also mints a value constructor of the same name — `["point", 1, 2]`, an inert tagged value for a nominal type, a checked identity for an alias — except for a `record` body, which mints none. Evaluates to `Nothing`.

operators.name: Element
operators.description:
Test whether a value is an element of a collection. Optional third argument is a boolean expression (condition) for filtered iteration in Sum/Product.

Element supports two modes of operation:
1. Set membership: Element(3, [List, 1, 2, 3]) checks if 3 is in the list
2. Type-style membership: Element(x, integer) checks if x has type integer

Type-style membership works with:

operators.name: Field

Access a named field of a value: `p.x` in Epsil.

On a value of a NOMINAL type whose definition body has named fields (a record body, or a named-tuple body), the field is resolved through the type definition — the sanctioned accessor window of the nominal-types design (D6/§4.5b D16). This does not make the value a collection: `First(p)` and `p["x"]` keep rejecting.

free variables of `fs` are used, in lexicographic order.

operators.description: Return the modular multiplicative inverse of `a` modulo `m`: the integer `x` in [0, m) with `a·x ≡ 1 (mod m)`. Undefined when `a` and `m` are not coprime.

operators.name: MoebiusMu
operators.description: Return the Möbius function μ(n): 0 if `n` is divisible by a perfect square > 1, otherwise (-1) raised to the number of distinct prime factors. The sign of `n` is ignored.

operators.name: Most
operators.signature: ((T) -> T where T: string) & ((indexed_collection<T>) -> list<T> where T)
operators.description:
Return the collection without the last element.

If the collection has only one element, return an empty collection.

operators.name: Multinomial
operators.description: Compute the multinomial coefficient for multiple integers.

operators.name: MultiplicativeOrder
operators.description: The multiplicative order of `a` modulo `n`: the smallest `k > 0` such that `a^k ≡ 1 (mod n)`. Undefined unless `a` and `n` are coprime.

operators.name: Multiply
operators.description: Product of two or more values.

operators.name: N
operators.description:
N(expr): numerically evaluate an expression

N(expr, precision): evaluate to `precision` significant digits

operators.name: NamedArgument
operators.description:
NamedArgument(name, value): one named argument of a call (Epsil

surface syntax: `f(rate: 0.05)`).

A parse-level carrier, like `Spread`, but one that never survives:

the enclosing call consumes it at canonicalization, permuting the

written arguments into the order its callee declares.

Reaching this definition therefore means the carrier was NOT

consumed — the callee supplied no parameter names to match — which

is the `argument-names-unavailable` error.

operators.name: Nand
operators.description: Logical NAND: the negation of AND (n-ary). Short-circuits: operands are evaluated left to right and evaluation stops at the first `False`.

operators.name: ND
operators.description: Numerical derivative evaluated at a point.

operators.name: NDSolve
operators.description: Numerical differential equation solver.

operators.name: NDSolveFunction
operators.description: Numerically solve an ordinary differential equation and return the solution as an applicable function (a `Function` literal wrapping an `InterpolatingFunction`), usable at any point of the integration interval. Same arguments as `NDSolve`, without the sample count.

operators.name: Negate
operators.description: Additive Inverse

operators.name: NextPrime
operators.description: Return the smallest prime greater than `n`. With a second argument `k`, return the kth prime after `n` (`k < 0` returns the |k|th prime before `n`).

operators.name: NIntegrate
operators.description: Numerical approximation of a definite integral.

operators.name: NLimit
operators.description: Numerical approximation of the limit of a function

operators.name: Nor
operators.description: Logical NOR: the negation of OR (n-ary). Short-circuits: operands are evaluated left to right and evaluation stops at the first `True`.

operators.name: Norm
operators.description: Vector or matrix norm.

operators.name: Normal
operators.description: Strip Big-O remainder terms from a series, yielding the truncated polynomial. Example: Normal(Series(\sin x, x)) → x - x^3/6 + x^5/120

operators.name: NormalDistribution
operators.description: Normal (Gaussian) distribution with mean μ and standard deviation σ.

operators.name: Not
operators.description: Logical negation (NOT).

operators.name: NotApprox
operators.description: Negated approximate-equality relation (not approximately equal).

operators.name: NotApproxEqual
operators.description: Negated approximately-equal relation.

operators.name: NotApproxNotEqual
operators.description: Negated approximately-not-equal relation.

operators.name: NotDivides
operators.description: `NotDivides(a, b)` returns `True` if `a` does not divide `b`, corresponding to the notation `a ∤ b`.

operators.name: NotElement
operators.description: Test whether a value is not an element of a collection.

operators.name: NotEqual
operators.description: Inequality comparison (not equal to).

operators.name: NotExists
operators.description: Negated existential quantifier (there does not exist): true when the predicate holds for no value.

operators.name: NotForAll
operators.description: Negated universal quantifier (not for all): true when the predicate fails for at least one value.

operators.name: NotGreater
operators.description: Negated greater-than relation (not greater than).

operators.name: NotGreaterNotEqual
operators.description: Neither greater than nor equal to.

operators.name: NotLess
operators.description: Negated less-than relation (not less than).

operators.name: NotLessNotEqual
operators.description: Neither less than nor equal to.

operators.name: NotPrecedes
operators.description: Negated precedes relation (does not precede).

operators.name: NotSubset
operators.description: Test whether the first collection is not a strict subset of the second.

operators.name: NotSucceeds
operators.description: Negated succeeds relation (does not succeed).

operators.name: NotSuperset
operators.description: Test whether the first collection is not a strict superset of the second.

operators.name: NotSupersetEqual
operators.description: Test whether the first collection is not a superset (possibly equal) of the second.

operators.name: NotTilde
operators.description: Negated similarity relation (not similar).

operators.name: NotTildeEqual
operators.description: Negated approximately/asymptotically-equal relation (not approximately equal).

operators.name: NotTildeFullEqual
operators.description: Negated isomorphism/congruence relation (not isomorphic or congruent).

operators.name: NPartition
operators.description: Number of integer partitions of n.

operators.name: NthPrime
operators.description: Return the nth prime number (1-based): `NthPrime(1)` is 2, `NthPrime(2)` is 3, …

operators.name: NumberFrom
operators.description:
NumberFrom(s): the number the string `s` denotes — optional surrounding whitespace, an optional sign, then ASCII digits with an optional "." fraction and an optional e/E exponent, or one of "oo", "+oo", "-oo", "NaN". The integer part may be omitted before a fraction (".5" is 0.5); a trailing "." with no fraction digits ("5.") is not accepted. Any other text, including "", is an error value (never NaN).

NumberFrom(s, base): the integer `s` denotes in `base` (2 to 36); only integer numerals are accepted.

operators.name: Numerator
operators.description: Numerator of an expression

operators.name: NumeratorDenominator
operators.description: Sequence of Numerator and Denominator of an expression

operators.name: Object
operators.description: Provenance head for the snapshot of a mutable object: `["Object", <record>, "'TypeName'"]`. The record holds the object's stored fields at the moment it was serialized; the second operand names the nominal type the object had. Not a constructor and not an ascription — it wraps data, it does not make an object.

operators.name: Oklab
operators.description: OKLab color (L 0-1, a/b ~ -0.4..0.4, optional alpha)

operators.name: Oklch
operators.description: OKLCh color (L 0-1, C 0-~0.4, hue degrees, optional alpha)

operators.name: OnesMatrix
operators.description: Matrix filled with ones.

operators.name: Or
operators.description: Logical disjunction (OR): true when at least one operand is true. Short-circuits: operands are evaluated left to right and evaluation stops at the first `True`.

operators.name: Ordering
operators.signature: (indexed_collection<T>, order: (((T) any -> unknown) | ((any, any) any -> number))?) -> list<integer> where T
operators.description: Return the indexes that would sort the collection.

operators.name: OverParen
operators.description: Over-paren accent (`\overparen{BC}`) — opaque typed head; not evaluated.

operators.name: PadEnd
operators.description: PadEnd(s, n, pad=" "): `s` padded at the END to `n` characters by repeating `pad` (its final copy truncated on a character boundary). Returned unchanged when `s` already has `n` or more characters. `n` must be a non-negative integer; an empty `pad` is an error; a non-string `pad` leaves the expression unevaluated.

operators.name: PadStart
operators.description: PadStart(s, n, pad=" "): `s` padded at the START to `n` characters by repeating `pad` (its final copy truncated on a character boundary). Returned unchanged when `s` already has `n` or more characters. `n` must be a non-negative integer; an empty `pad` is an error; a non-string `pad` leaves the expression unevaluated.

operators.name: Pair
operators.signature: (first: T, second: U) -> tuple<T, U> where T, U
operators.description: A tuple of two elements

operators.name: Parallel
operators.description: Parallelism relation (`AB \parallel CD`) — opaque typed head; not evaluated.

operators.name: Parse
operators.description: Parse a LaTeX string and evaluate to a corresponding expression

operators.name: PartialFraction
operators.description: Decompose a rational expression into partial fractions. Example: PartialFraction(1/((x+1)(x+2)), x) → 1/(x+1) - 1/(x+2)

operators.name: Partition
operators.signature: (collection<T>, integer | ((T) any -> boolean), integer?) -> list<list<T>> where T
operators.description:
Partition a collection into consecutive chunks each of size `n`; the trailing chunk may be shorter when `n` does not divide the length.

With a third argument `step`, produce sliding windows of length `n` whose starts are `step` apart, keeping only complete windows.

With a predicate function instead of an integer, split into two groups: elements for which the predicate is true, and those for which it is false.

Asymmetry: with no `step`, the trailing partial chunk is included; with an explicit `step`, only complete windows are returned.

See `Chunk` for splitting into a given number of nearly-equal groups.

operators.name: PDF
operators.description: Probability density (continuous) or mass (discrete) function of a distribution, evaluated at x.

operators.name: Permutations
operators.signature: ((S, integer?) -> list<string> where S: string) & ((collection, integer?) -> list<list>)
operators.description: Return all permutations of length k (default full length) of a collection.

operators.name: Perpendicular
operators.description: Perpendicularity relation (`AB \perp CD`) — opaque typed head; not evaluated.

operators.name: Pin
operators.description: Inside a `Match` pattern, `Pin(expr)` matches the value of `expr` (evaluated at match time) rather than its structure.

operators.name: Pipe
operators.description: Apply a function to a value: `Pipe(x, f)` evaluates to `f(x)`.

operators.name: PlusMinus
operators.signature: (T, U) -> tuple<T, U> where T: value, U: value
operators.description: Plus or Minus

operators.name: Pochhammer
operators.description: Rising factorial (Pochhammer symbol) (a)_k = a(a+1)…(a+k-1).

operators.name: PointList
operators.description: A list of points: zips collection components into a List of point-tuples (Desmos point-list idiom); a plain point when no component is a collection.

operators.name: PointX
operators.description: The x-coordinate of a point, broadcasting over a list of points.

operators.name: PointY
operators.description: The y-coordinate of a point, broadcasting over a list of points.

operators.name: PointZ
operators.description: The z-coordinate of a point, broadcasting over a list of points.

operators.name: PoissonDistribution
operators.description: Poisson distribution with rate parameter λ.

operators.name: PolyGamma
operators.description: Polygamma function, the n-th derivative of the digamma function

operators.name: Polygon
operators.description: Polygon primitive — opaque typed head.

operators.name: PolyLog
operators.description: Polylogarithm Liₛ(z) = Σ_{k≥1} zᵏ/kˢ.

operators.name: Polynomial
operators.description: Construct a polynomial from a list of coefficients (highest to lowest degree) and a variable. Example: Polynomial([1, 0, 2, 1], x) → x³ + 2x + 1

operators.name: PolynomialDegree
operators.description: Return the degree of a polynomial with respect to a variable. Example: PolynomialDegree(x³ + 2x + 1, x) → 3

operators.name: PolynomialFit
operators.description: Least-squares polynomial fit of the given degree. Returns the ascending coefficient List(c0, …, c_deg), or the fitted expression if a trailing variable symbol is given.

operators.name: PolynomialGCD
operators.signature: (a: value, b: value, variable: symbol?) -> value
operators.description: Return the greatest common divisor of two polynomials. Example: PolynomialGCD(x² - 1, x - 1, x) → x - 1

operators.name: PolynomialQuotient
operators.signature: (dividend: value, divisor: value, variable: symbol?) -> value
operators.description: Return the quotient of polynomial division of dividend by divisor. Example: PolynomialQuotient(x³ - 1, x - 1, x) → x² + x + 1

operators.name: PolynomialRemainder
operators.signature: (dividend: value, divisor: value, variable: symbol?) -> value
operators.description: Return the remainder of polynomial division of dividend by divisor. Example: PolynomialRemainder(x³ + 2x + 1, x + 1, x) → -2

operators.name: PolynomialRoots
operators.description: Return the roots of a polynomial expression. Example: PolynomialRoots(x² - 5x + 6, x) → {2, 3}

operators.name: PopulationCovariance
operators.description: Population covariance (n denominator) of paired data, given as two equal-length collections or one collection of (x, y) pairs.

operators.name: PopulationStandardDeviation
operators.description: Population Standard Deviation of a collection of numbers.

operators.name: PopulationVariance
operators.description: Population variance of a collection of numbers.

operators.name: Position
operators.signature: (collection<T>, predicate: (T) any -> boolean) -> list<integer> where T
operators.description: Return a list of indexes of elements in the collection satisfying the predicate.

operators.name: Power
operators.description: Exponentiation: raise a base to a power.

operators.name: PowerMod
operators.description: Return `a^b mod m` (modular exponentiation). A negative `b` uses the modular inverse of `a`; the result is undefined when that inverse does not exist (i.e. when `a` and `m` are not coprime). The result is in the range [0, m).

operators.name: PowerSet
operators.description: Return the power set of a set (set of all subsets).

operators.name: Precedes
operators.description: Precedes relation in an ordering (comes before).

operators.name: PreDecrement
operators.description: Decrement a number by one.

operators.name: Predicate
operators.description: Apply a predicate to arguments, returning a boolean

operators.name: PreIncrement
operators.description: Increment a number by one.

operators.name: Prime
operators.description: Derivative or prime notation (`f'`, `f^{(n)}`) — opaque typed head until a derivative library handler runs.

operators.name: PrimeFactors
operators.description: Return the sorted list of distinct prime factors of an integer `n`. The sign of `n` is ignored; `PrimeFactors(1)` is the empty list.

operators.name: PrimeImplicants
operators.description: Find all prime implicants using Quine-McCluskey. Max 12 variables.

operators.name: PrimeImplicates
operators.description: Find all prime implicates using Quine-McCluskey. Max 12 variables.

operators.name: PrimeNu
operators.description: Return ω(n), the number of distinct prime factors of `n`. The sign of `n` is ignored; `PrimeNu(1)` is 0.

operators.name: PrimeNumber
operators.description: The nth prime number. `PrimeNumber` is an alias for `NthPrime`, which is the preferred name.

operators.name: PrimeOmega
operators.description: Return Ω(n), the number of prime factors of `n` counted with multiplicity. The sign of `n` is ignored; `PrimeOmega(1)` is 0.

operators.name: PrimePi
operators.description: Return π(n), the prime-counting function: the number of primes less than or equal to `n`.

operators.name: PrimitiveRoot
operators.description: The smallest primitive root modulo `n` (a generator of the multiplicative group of integers mod `n`), or undefined if none exists (which happens unless `n` is 1, 2, 4, pᵏ, or 2pᵏ for an odd prime p).

operators.name: print
operators.description: Lowercase alias for `Print` (the Epsil command spelling); canonicalizes to `Print`.

operators.name: Print
operators.description: Print the operands to the host console, separated by spaces and followed by a newline. String operands print their content (without quotes); other expressions print their text form. Evaluates to `Nothing`. On a host without a console, prints nothing.

operators.name: Product
operators.description: `Product(f, a, b)` computes the product of `f` from `a` to `b`

operators.name: ProtocolMember
operators.signature: (protocol: string, member: string, arguments: any*) -> unknown
operators.description: Invoke a protocol member on a value — the lowering of a QUALIFIED protocol call (`Comparable.compare(x, y)` in Epsil, which parses as `Apply(Field(Comparable, "compare"), x, y)`). The first two operands name the protocol and the member; the rest are the call arguments. Dispatch is dynamic and restricted to the named protocol: the most specific conformance implementation for the runtime type of the first argument is invoked. Several equally specific implementations are `protocol-call-ambiguous`; none is `protocol-implementation-missing`; an argument whose type cannot decide the question leaves the call symbolic.

operators.name: ProtocolProperty
operators.signature: (protocol: string, property: string, receiver: any, value: any?) -> unknown
operators.description: Read (or write) a protocol PROPERTY through a NAMED protocol — the lowering of the qualified field form `person.(Nameable.name)` (protocols design P6, amending the D16 field grammar). The first two operands name the protocol and the property; the third is the receiver. A fourth operand makes it a property STORE — the qualified write `person.(Nameable.name) = v` — which invokes the `set` accessor against the receiver, discards what it returns, and evaluates to the value assigned; a receiver that is not an object is `immutable-value-assignment`. Dispatch is dynamic and restricted to the named protocol: the most specific conformance implementation for the runtime type of the receiver is invoked.

operators.name: PseudoInverse
operators.description: Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse of a matrix.

operators.name: QRDecomposition
operators.description: QR decomposition of a matrix.

operators.name: Quadrilateral
operators.description: Quadrilateral mark (`\square ABCD`) — opaque typed head; not evaluated.

operators.name: Quantile
operators.description: Quantile (inverse CDF): the least x with CDF(x) ≥ p, for p in [0, 1]. The first argument may also be a data collection, in which case the empirical quantile is returned.

operators.name: Quantity
operators.description: A value paired with a physical unit

operators.name: QuantityMagnitude
operators.description: Extract the numeric value from a quantity

operators.name: QuantityUnit
operators.description: Extract the unit from a quantity

operators.name: Quartiles
operators.description: Lower quartile, median, and upper quartile of a collection. Uses the Moore–McCabe (exclusive-hinges) convention: the sample is split at its median, and Q1/Q3 are the medians of the lower/upper halves with the overall median excluded from both halves when the sample size is odd.

operators.name: QuotientRing
operators.description:
The quotient of a ring by the ideal generated by the second argument.

`QuotientRing(Integers, n)` is ℤ/nℤ, the integers modulo `n`.

Inert: the residues are not enumerated, and membership is not decided.

operators.name: Radical
operators.description: Return the radical of `n` (its square-free kernel): the product of its distinct prime factors. The sign of `n` is ignored; `Radical(1)` is 1.

operators.name: Random
operators.description:
Random(): non-deterministic real in [0, 1)

Random(Interval(a, b)): a real in [a, b) (endpoint markers ignored)

Random(Range(...)): an element of the range

Random(xs): an element of the finite collection `xs`

operators.name: RandomChoice
operators.description: RandomChoice(domain, k): a list of k independent draws from `domain`, with replacement. `k` may exceed the size of the domain — that is what replacement means.

operators.name: RandomExpression
operators.description: Generate a random expression.

operators.name: RandomPrime
operators.description: Return a random prime. `RandomPrime(n)` draws a prime in [2, n]; `RandomPrime(m, n)` draws a prime in [m, n]. Undefined if the range contains no prime.

operators.name: RandomSample
operators.signature: ((T, number) random -> T where T: string) & ((indexed_collection, number) random -> list)
operators.description: RandomSample(xs, k): a list of k elements drawn from the indexed collection `xs`, without replacement. "Without replacement" is over POSITIONS, not values: on a multiset, repeats are expected — RandomSample([1, 1, 2], 2) can return [1, 1]. Sampling a string yields a string. Wrap the call in `WithRandomSeed(seed, ...)` to make it deterministic.

operators.name: RandomShuffle
operators.signature: ((T) random -> T where T: string) & ((indexed_collection<T>) random -> list<T> where T)
operators.description: Randomize the order of the elements in the collection. Shuffling a string yields a string. Wrap the call in `WithRandomSeed(seed, ...)` to make it deterministic.

operators.name: Range
operators.description: A sequence of numbers from a start to an end value with an optional step.

operators.name: RangeOf
operators.signature: (indexed_collection<T>, indexed_collection<T>, from: integer?) -> range | nothing where T
operators.description:
Return the 1-based inclusive index span of the first occurrence of `needle` as a contiguous subsequence of the indexed collection, or `Nothing` when it does not occur.

The search starts at index `from` (1 by default) and the span is always expressed in the original collection's indices, so `RangeOf(xs, needle, Last(r) + 1)` finds the next non-overlapping occurrence and the loop ends at `Nothing`.

On a string the needle is matched character by character, so a match never begins or ends inside a grapheme cluster.

operators.name: Rank
operators.description: The length of the shape of the expression. Note this is not the matrix rank (the number of linearly independent rows or columns in the matrix)

operators.name: Rational
operators.description: Construct a rational number from a numerator and denominator.

operators.name: Rationalize
operators.description: Approximate a real number by a rational. With a second argument `tolerance`, return the rational with the smallest denominator that approximates the number to within `tolerance` (a continued-fraction convergent); with no tolerance, rationalize at full working precision, as single-argument `Rational`.

operators.name: Real
operators.description: Real part of a complex number.

operators.name: Reduce
operators.signature: (collection<T>, reducer: (unknown, T) any -> unknown, initial: value?) -> value where T
operators.description: Reduce (fold) a collection to a single value by repeatedly applying a binary function, with an optional initial value.

operators.name: RegExp
operators.description:
A compiled regular expression, using the host JavaScript dialect.

The pattern is written most readably as a raw string literal: `RegExp(#"[0-9]+"#)`.

operators.name: ReleaseHold
operators.description: Release an expression held by `Hold`

operators.name: Remainder
operators.description: IEEE remainder: the signed remainder after dividing x by y, with the quotient rounded to the nearest integer (ties round toward +Infinity, matching JavaScript `Math.round`)

operators.name: Repeat
operators.description: Produce a sequence by repeating a single value. With 1 argument, returns an infinite sequence; with 2 arguments (value, count), returns a finite list of `count` copies.

operators.name: ReplaceAll
operators.description:
ReplaceAll(expr, rules): apply one or more replacement rules to `expr`,

then evaluate the result (Mathematica `expr /. rules`).

A rule is `lhs -> rhs` (parsed as `To`) or `Rule(lhs, rhs)`. Several

rules may be given as extra arguments or as a `List`/`Set` of rules;

they are applied simultaneously in a single pass.

operators.name: ReplaceAt
operators.description:
Return a copy of the indexed collection with the element at the 1-based `index` replaced by `value`.

A negative index counts from the end. An out-of-range, zero, or non-integer index leaves the expression unevaluated.

operators.name: Reshape
operators.description: Reshape a tensor or collection to a target shape.

operators.name: Residue
operators.description: Residue of a function at a point (the coefficient of (x-a)⁻¹ in its Laurent expansion)

operators.name: Rest
operators.signature: ((T) -> T where T: string) & ((indexed_collection<T>) -> list<T> where T)
operators.description:
Return the collection without the first element.

If the collection has only one element, return an empty collection.

operators.name: Resultant
operators.signature: (a: value, b: value, variable: symbol?) -> value
operators.description: Return the resultant of two polynomials with respect to a variable. It is zero iff the polynomials share a common factor. Example: Resultant(x² - 1, x - 1, x) → 0

operators.name: Reverse
operators.signature: ((T) -> T where T: string) & ((T) -> T where T: list) & ((indexed_collection<T>) -> list<T> where T)
operators.description: Reverse the order of the elements of an indexed collection.

operators.name: Rgb
operators.description: sRGB color (channels 0-1, optional alpha 0-1)

operators.name: Root
operators.description: n-th root of a value.

operators.name: RotateLeft
operators.signature: ((T, integer?) -> T where T: string) & ((T, integer?) -> T where T: list) & ((indexed_collection<T>, integer?) -> list<T> where T)
operators.description: Rotate the elements of the collection to the left by n positions.

operators.name: RotateRight
operators.signature: ((T, integer?) -> T where T: string) & ((T, integer?) -> T where T: list) & ((indexed_collection<T>, integer?) -> list<T> where T)
operators.description: Rotate the elements of the collection to the right by n positions.

operators.name: Round
operators.description: Rounds a number to the nearest integer, or (with a precision argument) to `n` decimal places.

operators.name: RowReduce
operators.description: Reduced row echelon form (RREF) of a matrix.

operators.name: RSolve
operators.description: Symbolic recurrence equation solver.

operators.name: Rule
operators.signature: (match: expression, replace: expression, predicate: function?) -> expression
operators.description: Pattern replacement rule.

operators.name: Same
operators.description:
Structural identity comparison (Epsil `===`).

True iff every adjacent pair of operands is structurally identical.

operators.name: Scan
operators.signature: (collection<T>, reducer: (unknown, T) any -> unknown, initial: value?) -> indexed_collection where T
operators.description: Return the cumulative fold of a collection: a same-length collection whose k-th element is the running result of applying a binary function left to right (optionally seeded by an initial value).

operators.name: Sec
operators.description: Secant, the reciprocal of cosine.

operators.name: Sech
operators.description: Hyperbolic secant, the reciprocal of hyperbolic cosine.

operators.name: Second
operators.description: The second element of a collection.

operators.name: Segment
operators.description: Segment primitive — opaque typed head.

operators.name: Sequence
operators.description: Ordered sequence of expressions.

operators.name: Series
operators.description: Taylor series expansion of an expression about a point (or an asymptotic expansion at ±∞), including Laurent, Puiseux (fractional-power), and log-aware expansions at poles and branch points. Only essential singularities, irrational exponents, and nested/reciprocal logarithms are left unevaluated. Example: Series(\sin x, x) → x - x^3/6 + x^5/120 + O(x^7)

operators.name: Set
operators.description: An unordered collection of distinct elements (a set).

operators.name: SetFrom
operators.description: Create a set from the elements of a collection.

operators.name: SetMinus
operators.description: Return the set difference between the first set and subsequent values.

operators.name: Shape
operators.description: Return the shape tuple of an expression.

operators.name: Sigma0
operators.description: Number of positive divisors of n.

operators.name: Sigma1
operators.description: Sum of positive divisors of n.

operators.name: SigmaMinus1
operators.description: Sum of reciprocals of positive divisors of n.

operators.name: Sign
operators.description: Sign of a number: -1, 0, or 1.

operators.name: Signature
operators.description: Return the signature string of an operator.

operators.name: Simplify
operators.description:
Simplify(expr): simplify an expression.

Simplify(expr, assumptions): simplify under one or more boolean
